author: NESJohnny (Wikimedia Commons user; neither Evan Amos nor anyone else has a public-domain photo of an official DS game card on Commons, so this is the Acekard 2.1, a third-party card in the DS game card's shell)
pixellab: second pass (tools/ds_notch.py, then raw-2): image-to-pixelart v2, 160x151 from a 1280x1210 input, init_image_strength 250, fixer on, text_guidance_scale 8; finished with finish_nintendo.py --no-dehalo and ds_clean.py (glare specks on the shell removed, light rim kept on the outline). raw-1 (strength 150) kept glare streaks, raw-3 (default strength) turned the shell dark blue again
logos_removed: the whole Acekard sticker: its light part (acekard 2, ver 2.1, slogan) painted flat light grey as the label, its black lower part (www.acekard.com) repainted with the card's plastic; second pass: the official DS game card's 45-degree cut at the top right corner painted in before the conversion (the Acekard shell has no visible cut in the photo) and the Acekard's dark blue plastic made the dark grey of Nintendo's DS cards
